transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess the main thing is I feel like I’m always going from one thing to the next. Like I can’t really just sit still or idle, if that makes sense. Even when there’s technically nothing urgent happening, I feel like I need to be doing something or shifting to the next thing.

And with the new work setup, it’s just become harder to hide. Before, I could kind of manage it or at least cover it up better, but now it stands out more, and it’s been getting in the way enough that I figured I should talk to somebody about it.
Have you ever had a period when your mood was unusually high or energized compared with your normal self?

I don’t think so, not in the way you mean, I don’t think. I mean, I have times where I get keyed up or I’m more talkative if something is stressful or exciting, or if there’s a lot going on, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had a stretch where my mood was unusually high compared to my normal self.

I’m trying to think, because “energized” is a tricky word for me. I can feel restless or like I need to keep moving, but that doesn’t really feel like a great mood or like I’m on top of the world or anything. It’s more just… I don’t settle very well. But as far as being unusually happy or elevated for a period of time, no, I haven’t really noticed that.
Looking back, were you already this restless or unable to settle as a child?

Yeah, looking back, I think it was there way before this recent job change. I didn’t really think of it that way at the time, because when you’re a kid you just think that’s how you are, but my old report cards were kind of a pattern.

Teachers would write things like I was bright, but careless, or that I needed reminders to stay with my work. And I remember comments about me talking out of turn, too. Not like I was trying to be difficult, exactly, but I’d just jump in or drift off from what I was supposed to be doing and then need to be brought back.

So, yeah, I’d say this isn’t something that just showed up recently. The work situation made it harder to cover, but the basic thing of not settling and needing reminders was there back in grade school.
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep popping into your mind even when you try to ignore them?

I’m not sure I’d say that, no. I mean, I do have thoughts pop in, like anybody does, and sometimes I’ll keep thinking about something I need to do or something I forgot, but I don’t think of them as unwanted thoughts in the sense that they’re disturbing or that I’m trying really hard to push them away and they keep coming back.

If you mean like a thought that feels intrusive or out of nowhere and really bothers me, I haven’t really noticed that as a big thing. For me it’s more that my mind moves around a lot, but not in a way where there’s one particular unwanted thought that keeps forcing itself in.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things?

I don’t think I worry excessively, no. I mean, I worry about normal things, like if something needs to get done or if there’s a bill or some issue at work, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around constantly worrying about everything.

Sometimes I’ll think, “Did I forget something?” or I’ll replay what I need to handle, but that feels more like trying to keep track of things than being consumed by worry. I don’t usually have this ongoing feeling that everyday things are going to go wrong. So, no, I wouldn’t describe myself as an excessive worrier.
